findings.trigger: Create q1 = TaskQueue(2) and q2 = TaskQueue(2), then call q1.put("a").
findings.observed: q2 also has length 1 and q2.get() returns "a".
findings.expected: q2 remains empty because separate TaskQueue instances must be independent.
findings.explanation: The mutable default items list is created once and reused by every construction that omits items, so those instances share the same backing queue. Allocate a fresh list per instance instead.

findings.trigger: Create TaskQueue(1), put("kept"), then call put("rejected") and catch OverflowError.
findings.observed: After OverflowError, the queue length is 2; successive get() calls return "kept" and then "rejected".
findings.expected: The queue remains length 1 and contains only "kept" because a full put must not change queued items.
findings.explanation: put appends before checking capacity and never rolls the append back when raising. Check capacity before mutating the list (or undo the append before raising).
